status: Beats no skill and the comparison skill on total and on traps, on both models (final round: Haiku 64/64, Opus 63/64). Not fully met on one point: in the final round Opus made two unsupported statements (that Search Partners spend sat inside the waste total, and a cause for junk terms the data didn't show). The wording that invited the first is fixed in 1.2.1 (text only, not re-tested). No invented dollar figures, benchmarks, forecasts or account changes in any with-skill run.
method: 8 evals (4 traps), 64 expectations written before any run, on fictional accounts (Tallyhouse, Quillmetrics with brand memory; Ferncliff and Pipewise without). Round 1 ran the skill, no skill and the comparison skill (Corey Haines' paid-ads 1.1.0) on Haiku, and the skill and no skill on Opus, in fresh headless agents graded blind by a separate Opus grader. One invalid no-skill Haiku run (it failed to see its input files) was re-run and re-graded. Rounds 2 and 3 re-ran the revised skill (round 3 on Haiku and Opus).
losses_and_open_issues: Round 3, Opus, eval 5: the explanation for declining the 500% ROAS line ran to five sentences (limit three)

Round 3, Opus, eval 4: said the $61.40 Search Partners spend 'is already inside' the $277.50 waste total; the export doesn't show that (Haiku said 'overlaps' more loosely). Wording fixed in 1.2.1, not re-tested
Round 3, Opus, eval 1: stated Smart Bidding as the cause of junk searches getting through, a guess presented as fact
Round 3, Opus, eval 7: fixes.md suggested pausing 'restaurant cpa', whose search terms brought 9 conversions, while the reply said not to pause keywords
Round 3, Haiku, eval 5: top three said exclude four countries; the 48-hour plan said confirm Canada and the UK first
Round 2, Haiku: added 'tally house' as a brand term that appears nowhere in the data; borderline calls ('restaurant pos systems', 'stripe fees calculator') varied between runs on the same exports

Round 1, Haiku with skill: compared a budget-limited campaign with the blended CPA and said hold the budget (fixed in 1.1.0); gave a report location for only one export (fixed); left script and working-file names in client files (fixed)

Round 1, without the skill: no-skill Opus and the comparison skill both annualized 10 days of data (about $10,100 a year) and gave a verdict on Target CPA from 4 conversions; every non-skill run offered a substitute ROAS or CPA forecast in the ROAS trap; no-skill Opus claimed a headline came from brand files when it didn't; the comparison skill leaked its own name and tool paths
In this environment a user-level instruction made one Opus run open with the skill's name; end clients would see it
Every run, all configs, left the original export and brand files unchanged; no run claimed to change the account
